title: Interactive run-inspector: dry-run, permissioned actions, and telemetry bridge for admin tasks
creator: Aisha Kapoor
description:
Summary:
We need an interactive 'run-inspector' UX and backend that lets oncall and support engineers preview, validate, and execute runbook tasks with a safe dry-run mode, permissioned action gating, and a telemetry bridge that streams step-level metrics into the Console. The feature should treat runbooks-as-tasks as first-class objects: display inputs, resolve secrets via KMS integration, show expected side-effects, and provide a reversible dry-run that simulates resource changes without performing them.

Motivation:
1) Reduce time-to-remediation by giving engineers a single surface to evaluate a runbook's effects before running it.
2) Reduce blast radius by making permission checks and approval flows explicit at each actionable step.
3) Improve post-incident analysis by surfacing structured telemetry (duration, cost tokens, KV cache hits, API fallback counts) per step to the Console.

Scope & non-goals:
Scope: interactive web inspector, dry-run simulator, step-level permission gating, telemetry event hooks, audit log integration, CLI flag parity (opsctl --inspect).
Non-goals: fully authored runbook editor (we'll link to the existing runbook authoring MVP), long-term RBAC policy language redesign (that's a follow-up).
acceptance_criteria: Web inspector shows the expanded task graph with step inputs, outputs, and estimated side-effects for at least three common admin playlets (restart-service, scale-pool, revoke-key)
Dry-run simulates effects without making state changes and produces a diff-style report saved to the audit log
Permission gating prevents execution of steps for users without required roles and surfaces a clear approval path
Telemetry bridge emits step-level events to the Console stream (trace id, step name, duration_ms, token_count_estimate, kv_cache_hit) and Dashboard shows them within 24 hours
CLI parity: opsctl inspect <playlet> returns same diff and simulation report as the Console inspector
All simulated runs are logged with a unique run-id and marked as simulation in the audit store
implementation_steps: Design API: /v1/playlets/:id/inspect -> returns step graph, estimated side-effects, required permissions
Backend simulator: sandbox runner that replays inputs against models and stubbed infra connectors to generate deterministic diffs
Permission layer: enforce per-step RBAC checks with explicit approval links and integration with SSO groups
Telemetry bridge: define event schema, wire to Console ingestion pipeline, create dashboard widgets for step-level metrics
UI surface: interactive inspector with expandable steps, dry-run button, approval CTA, and link to related PR/Confluence
CLI: add opsctl inspect with --dry-run and --explain flags to mirror Console behavior
Audit & compliance: persist simulation reports, approvals, and executed run metadata in the audit index
risks_and_mitigation: Risk: Simulator divergence from production behavior could provide false confidence -> Mitigation: enforce model/stub parity tests and include a confidence score in reports
Risk: Sensitive secrets exposure in the inspector -> Mitigation: redact secrets, fetch ephemeral tokens via KMS proxy, and require per-user view permission
Risk: Permission bypass bugs during rollout -> Mitigation: canary rollout with feature flag, mandatory security code review, and telemetry-based anomaly detection on approvals
